title: IP Find for Chrome
subtitle: Network IP Discovery Tool
description: One click and Chrome tells you your IP. A whole extension for something you could search for; in my defence, it is faster.
longDescription: A Chrome extension that quickly identifies and displays the current network's IP address. This tool is useful for network diagnostics and understanding your current network configuration.
mascotLines: It only asks for the clipboard. It couldn't peek at your tabs if it wanted to.
geoiplookup.io ignores ?ip= and tells you about yourself instead.
imageCaptions: The popup: your own IP on top, a lookup of 8.8.8.8 below, recent searches at the bottom
What leaves your browser: one request per lookup; history stays local, no tracking
why: "What's my IP?" comes back every time you switch VPN or Wi-Fi, usually with "and where does it think I am?" IP Find answers both from a toolbar popup and looks up any other address too. It asks for the clipboard and nothing else, so it couldn't read your pages even if it wanted to.
gains: It also answers the other usual question: whose IP is this? Paste one and get its city, ISP and AS number, the time there and a map link, with the last six lookups a click away. A 192.168 address is told plainly it isn't on the map, not handed an empty card.
lessons: geoiplookup.io ignores an ?ip= query and answers with your own IP instead, so the address to look up has to go in the URL path.
Private and reserved ranges come back as HTTP 200 with success: false, so 'no data' is read from the body, not the status code.
The API stopped sending current_time, so the popup now works out the local time from the timezone name by itself.
